source.evidence: Table 7 official blind evaluation and section 4.3.2 boundary limitations

purpose: Turn the published DX2026 boundary failures into explicit synthetic falsification cases for behavioral-set diagnosis, unknown rejection and regime-conditioned calibration. These cases do not reproduce the paper or use its raw waveforms.

cases.paper_explanation: The authors state that this negative intake-manifold pressure drift became indistinguishable from natural model uncertainty during frequent low-load deceleration phases.
cases.acceptance: Retain the true fault inside the admissible set; report ambiguity rather than forcing normal or a unique fpim cause where the supported behavioral envelopes overlap.

cases.paper_explanation: The identical fault magnitude is highly detectable under highway conditions, demonstrating that diagnostic separability is operating-regime dependent.

synthetic_behavioral_set_fixture.uniqueness_scope: within the exact frozen highway-regime catalogue only

cases.acceptance: A regime-specific catalogue may distinguish the fault when the measured interval is disjoint from the normal envelope; do not transfer that uniqueness to FTP75 Standard.

cases.paper_explanation: The authors report all anomalies detected but the symptom vector falls outside their fault-signature matrix, collapsing isolation accuracy to zero while false alarms are high.
cases.acceptance: A detector may flag a strong anomaly while the isolator refuses to invent a known cause. Preserve an explicit unknown/out-of-support disposition and do not relabel it as a correct fault isolation.

cross_case_invariants: The standard and highway fpim -10% cases have separate regime IDs and separately calibrated envelopes.
Calibration data for each regime are disjoint from the confirmatory recording.
The true reference fault identity remains evaluator-only; it is never exposed to the inference module.
A singleton is unique only within the declared regime and catalogue; global physical uniqueness is never implied.
Unknown/out-of-support is counted separately from detection failure and false alarm.
The published numbers are external baseline values, not reproduced Symtropy performance.

research_targets_not_achieved.target: At least 95% of independently annotated fault cases retain the true fault in the admissible set at the preregistered marginal coverage level, with recording-clustered uncertainty.
Zero forced singleton causes when the reference calibrated behavioral envelopes overlap or the case is outside every supported envelope.
For the published WLTP fpic +8% failure mode, flag the anomaly while preserving unknown/out-of-support rather than assigning an unsupported known cause.
The same fpim -10% fault is allowed to be ambiguous in FTP75 Standard and uniquely identifiable within the separate FTP75 Highway catalogue, without cross-regime leakage.

claim_ceiling: Synthetic envelope counterexamples and protocol checks only. No LiU-ICE waveforms, model, or published solution have been reproduced by these fixtures.
